newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen flat to lower before expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen flat to lower before expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to lower Friday ahead of May contracts' expiration this afternoon.
"They were up and now they are coming down hard," said an East Coast paper broker, referring to May and June futures prices in over-the-counter trading.

May OTC California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $14.00-14.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursday's settlement at $13.90, while May OTC Palo Verde at $18.00-18.15 against yesterday's close at $17.98.
June COB and PV futures, in the paper market, were assessed at $12.90-13.15 and $18.40-18.75, respectively.

Market sources said players would be closely following the natural gas prices, physical power values in the West, hydroelectric output in the Northwest and offers from Bonneville Power Administration.
NYMEX June Henry Hub futures were up 4.3 cents at $2.165 per million British thermal units in early activity.
Western cash power prices have slid this week on moderate weather and generating capacity returning to service from repair and maintenance outages.

Nevertheless, the spring plant maintenance season is still in full swing. A number of units were heard shutting this weekend including a 700 megawatt (MW) unit at the Colstrip coal-fired complex in Montana and a 550 MW unit at the Laramie River Station in Wyoming.

The Western Systems Coordinating Council's board was said to have decided on raising the transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie for the spring from the current 6,250 MW. The board's decision could not immediately be confirmed.
Meteorologists said temperatures in the Northwest would average above normal this weekend into early next week, while in the Southwest, readings would moderate to near normal levels regionwide.
The northern and eastern sections of the Southwest would continue to see cloudy skies with showers and thunderstorms in the valleys and snow in the upper mountains through tomorrow.

Coastal centers like Portland and San Francisco are expected to enjoy mostly mild, sunny weather this weekend with temperatures peaking in the 60s-70s F. Main Southwest cities like Phoenix, Las Vegas and Los Angeles are predicted to hit day peaks in the 80s-90s F.
